s1.syndrome_frame: Episodic hypertension with micturition-related syncope and symptoms of catecholamine excess
salient_findings: Micturition-related episodes of headaches, diaphoresis, palpitations, chest pain, and presyncope
Tachycardia and significant blood pressure lability
Elevated plasma free metanephrine levels and isolated normetanephrine elevation in 24-hour urinary metanephrines
Bilateral crackles on pulmonary examination and pink, frothy secretions from endotracheal tube
key_facts: 2-year history of episodic hypertension
Micturition-related syncope
Episodic chest pain, palpitations, and diaphoresis
Tachycardia with a heart rate of 112 beats/min
Blood pressure of 196/120 mmHg
High-sensitivity troponin T of 936 ng/L, peaked at 1026 ng/L
N-terminal pro-BNP of 49 pg/mL
Plasma free metanephrine levels with isolated elevation in plasma normetanephrine (36 nmol/L)
24-hour urinary metanephrines with isolated normetanephrine elevation (8990 mcg)
Free norepinephrine of 21,685 pg/mL
Mildly depressed left ventricular systolic function (EF 40-45%) with hypokinesis of septum and inferolateral wall
Bilateral hilar opacities suggesting acute pulmonary edema on chest radiography
1.9 cm × 2.8 cm contrast-enhancing mass in bladder wall with surrounding lymphadenopathy on CT abdomen

shortlist.label: Bladder paraganglioma
shortlist.why_kept: Micturition-related symptoms and catecholamine excess with a bladder mass on CT abdomen

shortlist.label: Pheochromocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Episodic hypertension, elevated plasma and urinary metanephrines, and symptoms of catecholamine excess

shortlist.label: Paraganglioma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to pheochromocytoma, with possible extra-adrenal location

shortlist.label: Catecholamine-induced cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Mildly depressed left ventricular systolic function and symptoms of catecholamine excess

shortlist.label: Hypertensive crisis
shortlist.why_kept: Severe hypertension with end-organ damage, including cardiac and pulmonary involvement

raw.rationale: The presence of a 1.9 cm × 2.8 cm contrast-enhancing mass in the bladder wall with surrounding lymphadenopathy on CT abdomen, along with the patient's symptoms of micturition-related syncope, episodic hypertension, and elevated plasma and urinary normetanephrine levels, strongly supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pheochromocytoma
rejected.why: Normal adrenal glands on CT abdomen make this less likely

rejected.label: Paraganglioma
rejected.why: While possible, the specific location of the tumor in the bladder wall points more towards bladder paraganglioma

rejected.label: Catecholamine-induced cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: This could be a consequence of the primary condition but does not explain the primary cause of the symptoms and lab findings

rejected.label: Hypertensive crisis
rejected.why: This is a symptom rather than a diagnosis and does not explain the underlying cause of the patient's condition

gold: Metastatic paraganglioma of the urinary bladder
